<a id="secrets"></a>
This catalog describes **interpretation coverage, not which resources are included in your architecture**. Managed and data instances present in a supported plan or state remain represented in the Form even when no selected Dialect or Rule interprets them. Rootform does not invent a classification, Context or Relation for them.

Presence in the Form does not imply a permanent card in every Explorer scene. [How Rootform works](../concepts.md#every-observed-instance-starts-with-a-representation) explains the distinction; [Explorer navigation](../guides/explore-architecture.md#reveal-a-secondary-resource) shows how to inspect secondary resources.

## Official Dialects

<a id="providers-and-versions"></a>
<a id="interpreted-types-and-declared-facts"></a>

Find your provider binding, then open its Dialect. A Dialect can bind more than one provider. A binding does not imply complete provider coverage; each constraint describes declared compatibility, not evidence that every provider version was tested. Rootform does not use an observed exact provider version to choose a Rule.

Dialect pages distinguish local vocabulary declarations, RF Vocabulary references and Rule behavior. Declared emissions and composition describe what a Rule can establish; each input must supply the evidence. Resource and data populations, conditions and independent composition members remain distinct. Presentation mappings supply visual identities, not architectural facts.

## Input limits

Plan JSON, state JSON and saved Forms are limited to 128 MiB per input. Rootform refuses an oversized input before loading the entire file. The [language limits](../language/reference/diagnostics.md#limits) apply separately to authored and compiled definitions.

[Choose an input](../inputs/index.md) covers accepted exports. [Plans and saved plans](../inputs/plans.md) covers pairing and reference evidence. [Select Dialects](../cli.md) covers local and OCI selections; this catalog describes the official embedded sources.
